answer: Coordination horizon pricing. Each agent publishes a walnut: a signed forecast of its own future action window. To coordinate, agents must align forecast horizons; mismatched windows incur a delay tax paid in credits. Sybils multiply identities but cannot fabricate consistent comet-like forecast trails without paying the delay tax per identity per cycle, and forged trails are cheaply audited against later behavior. Attacker cost scales with identity count times window mismatch, making mass coordination quadratically expensive without any locked capital.
